label: Cloze
description: Fill-the-blank single-word recall on high-yield evolution facts (Hardy-Weinberg, selection, drift, game theory, phylogeny, empirical case studies).

cards.term: The Hardy-Weinberg equation states that p² + 2pq + ____ = 1 for a biallelic locus.
Hardy-Weinberg requires no mutation, no migration, no selection, infinite population, and ____ mating.
If disease frequency is q² then carrier frequency is approximately ____.
For an X-linked recessive at frequency q, hemizygous males are affected at frequency ____.
Allele-frequency change in a finite population due to random sampling of gametes is called genetic ____.
In small populations, drift dominates over selection when |s| < 1/(2N), where N is the ____ population size.
Founder effect and bottleneck effect are two types of genetic ____.
Gene ____ is the movement of alleles between populations via migration of individuals or gametes.
Inbreeding raises homozygosity but does NOT change ____ frequencies (in the absence of selection).
The inbreeding coefficient ____ is the probability that two alleles at a locus are identical by descent.
Apparent heterozygote deficit caused by sampling across multiple subpopulations with different allele frequencies is the ____ effect.
Mutation alone changes allele frequencies extremely slowly because the rate is on the order of ____ per generation.
Natural selection requires variation, heritability, and differential ____ success.
The fraction of phenotypic variance attributable to additive genetic variance is the narrow-sense ____, h².
The breeder's equation predicts response to selection R = ____ × S, where S is the selection differential.
If h² is zero, R = 0 regardless of S because there is no ____ variation to inherit.
____ selection favors one extreme of a trait distribution and shifts the mean over generations.
____ selection reduces variance by favoring the average phenotype (e.g., human birth weight).
____ selection favors both extremes and can split a population (e.g., African seedcrackers).
Selection that favors heterozygotes over both homozygotes is called ____ vigor or overdominance (e.g., sickle-cell + malaria).
An evolutionarily stable strategy (____) cannot be invaded by a rare mutant strategy.
In Hawk-Dove with V < C, the ESS is a mixed strategy with the proportion of Hawks equal to ____.
When V ≥ C in Hawk-Dove, the pure ____ strategy is the ESS.
Hamilton's rule for the evolution of altruism states that an altruistic act spreads when rB > ____.
In Hamilton's rule, r is the coefficient of ____ between actor and recipient.
Two full siblings share, on average, ____ of their alleles identical by descent.
Reciprocal altruism between non-kin is stable when partners can recognize each other and ____ defectors.
Adaptations are favored by natural selection because they increase ____.
Fitness is best defined operationally as the expected number of ____ produced by an individual.
Sexual selection acts via mate ____ (intersexual) and male-male competition (intrasexual).
The 'handicap principle' (Zahavi) explains how costly ornaments can be ____ signals of male quality.
Anisogamy (different gamete sizes) is the original cause of sexual ____ between males and females.
A monophyletic group includes a common ancestor and ALL of its ____.
A group with the common ancestor but excluding some descendants (e.g., reptiles excluding birds) is ____.
A group of organisms grouped by shared traits that did NOT come from a common ancestor (e.g., flying vertebrates) is ____.
A shared derived character useful for grouping is a ____.
A shared ancestral character that does NOT inform grouping is a ____.
A trait independently evolved in two lineages (analogous, not homologous) is the result of ____ evolution.
On a phylogeny, two lineages that share their most recent common ancestor with each other are called ____ taxa.
____ selection by Grant & Grant produced larger beak sizes in Galápagos finches after the 1977 drought.
The shift from light to >95% melanic Biston betularia in industrial Britain is the classic ____ moth example.
Sickle-cell allele HbS persists at ~10% in malaria zones because heterozygotes have higher ____ against malaria.
Antibiotic resistance evolves within ~2 years of a new drug's clinical introduction because resistant mutants have higher ____.
Belyaev's silver fox experiment showed that selection for ____ rapidly produced dog-like coat patterns and tameness in just decades.
Trophy hunting of Alberta bighorn sheep over 30 years produced a 25% decline in horn ____ — a fishing/hunting selection example.
Atlantic cod under decades of size-limit fishing now mature smaller and ____ — a human-induced selection example.
Speciation that occurs WITHOUT geographic isolation (e.g., Lake Apoyo cichlids) is ____ speciation.
Speciation that requires geographic isolation followed by divergence is ____ speciation.
Reproductive isolating mechanisms that prevent fertilization (e.g., habitat, temporal, behavioral, mechanical, gametic) are ____ barriers.
Reproductive barriers that act after fertilization (e.g., hybrid inviability or sterility like the mule) are ____ barriers.
The biological species concept defines species as groups capable of interbreeding and producing fertile ____.
Long evolutionary 'stasis' punctuated by short bursts of rapid speciation is called ____ equilibrium.
MHC genes are the most ____ in the vertebrate genome because heterozygote advantage maintains many alleles.
Inbreeding depression is most severe in ____ isolated populations because deleterious recessives become homozygous.
